> Worked solutions for all 9 practice exercise options, in R. These reuse the
> exact approaches taught in the main workshop session. Run the data-loading
> chunk first, then jump to whichever option(s) you worked on.

## Load data

```{r load-data}
library(tidyverse)

clinical_r <- read_csv("clinical_trial_data.csv")
longitudinal_r <- read_csv("longitudinal_data.csv")
pca_data_r <- read_csv("pca_data.csv")

head(clinical_r)
```

---

## Option 1: Table 1 comparing baseline characteristics by arm

```{r option1}
library(gtsummary)

clinical_r %>%
  select(arm, sex, smoker, site, response_label, baseline_score, followup_score, age, biomarker) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = arm,
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 1
  ) %>%
  add_p(
    test = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "t.test",
      all_categorical() ~ "chisq.test"
    ),
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  bold_labels()
```

---

## Option 2: Density plot or ridgeline plot

Showing both — overlaid density by response label, and ridgeline by site.

```{r option2a, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
ggplot(clinical_r, aes(x = baseline_score, fill = response_label)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Baseline Score", y = "Density", fill = "Arm",
       title = "Baseline Score Distribution by Arm") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r option2b, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
library(ggridges)

ggplot(clinical_r, aes(x = baseline_score, y = site, fill = site)) +
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.7, scale = 1.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  labs(x = "Baseline Score", y = NULL, title = "Baeline Score Distribution by Site") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

---

## Option 3: Kaplan-Meier curve with risk table

```{r option3, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
library(survival)
library(survminer)

fit <- survfit(Surv(time_months, event) ~ arm, data = clinical_r)

ggsurvplot(
  fit,
  data = clinical_r,
  pval = TRUE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  palette = c("#440154", "#21908C"),
  xlab = "Time (months)",
  ylab = "Survival Probability",
  legend.title = "Arm",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
)
```

---

## Option 4: Forest plot across 3+ subgroups

```{r option4, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
forest_data_r <- tibble(
  subgroup = c("Overall", "Age under 58", "Age 58 plus", "Female", "Male"),
  hr = c(0.72, 0.65, 0.81, 0.70, 0.75),
  lower = c(0.55, 0.45, 0.58, 0.50, 0.52),
  upper = c(0.94, 0.93, 1.13, 0.98, 1.08)
) %>%
  mutate(subgroup = fct_rev(fct_inorder(subgroup)))

ggplot(forest_data_r, aes(x = hr, y = subgroup)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), height = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#21908C") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Hazard Ratio (log scale)", y = NULL, title = "Treatment Effect by Subgroup") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

---

## Option 5: ROC curve with AUC

```{r option5, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
library(pROC)

roc_obj_r <- roc(clinical_r$responder, clinical_r$biomarker, quiet = TRUE)
auc_val_r <- auc(roc_obj_r)

ggroc(roc_obj_r, color = "#21908C", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.3, y = 0.2, label = sprintf("AUC = %.3f", auc_val_r), size = 5) +
  labs(x = "Specificity", y = "Sensitivity", title = "ROC Curve: Biomarker Predicting Response") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

---

## Option 6: Line chart of score trajectory with error bars

```{r option6, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
summary_r <- longitudinal_r %>%
  group_by(arm, week) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(score),
    sd_score = sd(score),
    se_score = sd_score / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(summary_r, aes(x = week, y = mean_score, color = arm, group = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean_score - se_score, ymax = mean_score + se_score),
    width = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Week", y = "Mean Score (\u00b1 SE)", color = "Arm",
    title = "Score Trajectory Over Time by Arm"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

---

## Option 7: Annotated boxplot/mean+-SD bar comparing scores across site

Showing the ANOVA + pairwise comparison version across `site`, with
significance brackets, since this directly addresses "comparing scores
across site."

```{r option7}
anova_model <- aov(baseline_score ~ site, data = clinical_r)
anova_summary <- summary(anova_model)
anova_pvalue <- anova_summary[[1]][1, "Pr(>F)"]
cat("ANOVA p-value:", format.pval(anova_pvalue, digits = 4), "\n")

tukey_result <- TukeyHSD(anova_model)
print(tukey_result)

site_levels <- levels(factor(clinical_r$site))
comparisons_list <- combn(site_levels, 2, simplify = FALSE)
```

```{r option7-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
library(ggpubr)

ggplot(clinical_r, aes(x = site, y = baseline_score, fill = site)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_compare_means(
    method = "anova",
    label.y = max(clinical_r$followup_score) * 1.5,
    label.x = (length(site_levels) + 1) / 2,
    hjust = 0.5
  ) +
  stat_compare_means(
    comparisons = comparisons_list,
    method = "t.test",
    label = "p.signif",
    step.increase = 0.08,
    hide.ns = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.8) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Baseline Score", title = "Baseline Score by Site") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Option 8: Stacked bar chart of smoker status by site

```{r option8, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
smoker_summary_r <- clinical_r %>%
  mutate(smoker = factor(smoker, levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current"))) %>%
  count(site, smoker) %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))


ggplot(smoker_summary_r, aes(x = site, y = prop, fill = smoker)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1)),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white", size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#009E73", "#56B4E9", "#E69F00")) +  # Okabe-Ito
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion", fill = "Smoking Status",
       title = "Smoking Status Composition by Site") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

> **Note:** this uses a 3-category version of the stacked bar chart taught in
> the main workshop (which used 2 categories: Response/No Response). With 3
> categories, stacking is still readable; beyond ~4 categories, consider a
> grouped bar chart instead.

## Option 9: PCA score plot or biplot of the biomarker panel

```{r option9a, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
biomarker_cols <- paste0("marker_", 1:6)

pca_fit_r <- prcomp(pca_data_r[, biomarker_cols], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
var_explained_r <- (pca_fit_r$sdev^2) / sum(pca_fit_r$sdev^2) * 100

pc_scores_r <- as_tibble(pca_fit_r$x) %>%
  bind_cols(pca_data_r %>% select(arm, site))

ggplot(pc_scores_r, aes(x = PC1, y = PC3, color = arm)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75) +
  stat_ellipse(level = 0.95) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%% variance)", var_explained_r[1]),
    y = sprintf("PC3 (%.1f%% variance)", var_explained_r[3]),
    color = "Arm", title = "PCA of Biomarker Panel"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r option9b, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
loadings_r <- as_tibble(pca_fit_r$rotation[, 1:3], rownames = "biomarker")
scale_factor <- max(abs(pc_scores_r$PC1), abs(pc_scores_r$PC3)) * 0.8

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = pc_scores_r, aes(x = PC1, y = PC3, color = arm), size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(
    data = loadings_r,
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1 * scale_factor, yend = PC3 * scale_factor),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), color = "#D55E00"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = loadings_r,
    aes(x = PC1 * scale_factor * 1.15, y = PC3 * scale_factor * 1.15, label = biomarker),
    color = "#D55E00", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%% variance)", var_explained_r[1]),
    y = sprintf("PC3 (%.1f%% variance)", var_explained_r[3]),
    color = "Arm", title = "PCA Biplot: Scores + Biomarker Loadings"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
